context: Request: firm M&A matters in healthcare-services, biotech or pharma that used rep-and-warranty insurance, with policy documentation. Rubric: 1001-00003, 1001-00007, 1006-00008 (Crestline / Lakewood healthcare services), 1013-00006, 1018-00008 (Penterra, terminated but with a bound policy), a proof document for each, and a precision criterion.

first_error.critic_note: (generic flag) The next screening review at [91] said about 60 surfaced matters were never opened, with examples that did not include this matter; nothing named it.

other_errors.critic_note: (specific flag) The write review at [97] said the terminated deal's bound policy is not a completed matter and inflates the set; the agent moved it to a non-counted reference.
other_errors.why: The check stage moved a pharma acquisition with a bound policy out of the answer because the deal terminated before closing (evidence seen at [68]-[69]).

divergence: Mixed (T0 passes; T1 and T2 fail on the same healthcare-services acquisition, T2 also on a terminated pharma deal). The split is at the scan-to-candidate step. T0 completed a ranged store-wide scan and, after a review flagged its strict filter, rebuilt its own candidate list inclusively (agent-defined stage, attempt 2: 54 matters) and read about 20 candidates including that matter. T1's scans all timed out and it fell back on file names, which never showed the matter (the review named the incomplete scan; ignored). T2's agent-defined rescan did list the matter, but screening read eight others and no review named it. All three write reviews questioned the terminated deal; T2 demoted it to a non-counted reference and lost that criterion, T0 bucketed it separately but still described it as a precedent, and T1 kept it. Label notes played no role.
